source.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי֙ מֵעִ֣יר עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י לֵ֣ב קָמָ֑י ר֖וּחַ מַשְׁחִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Here I [am] stirring up against Babylon and against [the] inhabitants of Leb-qamai a wind of a destroyer.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Look, I am stirring up against Babylon \q and against the inhabitants of Leb-qamai \q a destroying wind.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q I am stirring up against Babylon \q and against the people who live in Leb-qamai \q a wind that destroys.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q I am about to send a destroying wind \q against Babylon and against the people of Leb-qamai, that is, the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: Leb-qamai: a coded name for the Chaldeans
alternatives: the heart of those who rise up against me
decisions.reason: Leb-qamai is "Chaldeans" written in a simple code called *atbash*, in which the first letter of the alphabet stands for the last, the second for the next to last, and so on. By that code the consonants of *Kasdim*, "Chaldeans", become those of Leb-qamai. The code itself makes words that mean "the heart of those who rise up against me", which fits a people who set themselves against God. The same code turns Babel into Sheshach (25:26; 51:41). Since Babylon is named openly in the same line, the code was probably not for secrecy; it may be a play on words or a mark of contempt. The Greek translation reads "the Chaldeans" here (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: a destroying wind: a wind that destroys, sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The word can mean wind or spirit, and the phrase could be read "the spirit of a destroyer", that is, God moving the mind of a conqueror, as in verse 11, where the LORD stirs up the spirit of the kings of the Medes. Here the winnowing of verse 2 favors a wind, the hot wind that blows away chaff (4:11-12; 13:24). Both readings say the same thing: the LORD himself sets Babylon's destruction in motion.

decisions.choice: look, I am stirring up: something the LORD is about to do
decisions.reason: The pointing word and the participle announce an act that is already beginning. The same verb returns in verse 11 for the kings of the Medes. The chapter continues the oracle against Babylon begun in 50:1.

decisions.choice: that is, the Babylonians
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the coded name and adds what it stands for, as in 25:26, since most readers would not recognize the code (m1). It says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, as Readable does throughout. Literal and Balanced keep the name alone, with the footnote.

source.text: וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֤ל׀זָרִים֙ וְזֵר֔וּהָ וִיבֹקְק֖וּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֑הּ כִּֽי־הָי֥וּ עָלֶ֛יהָ מִסָּבִ֖יב בְּי֥וֹם רָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will send to Babylon strangers and they will winnow her, and they will empty her land, for they will be against her from around on [the] day of disaster.

en.L: And I will send strangers to Babylon, and they will winnow her, \q and they will empty her land, \q for they will be against her from every side on the day of disaster.
en.B: I will send foreigners to Babylon to winnow her \q and to strip her land bare, \q for they will come against her from every side on the day of disaster.
en.R: I will send foreigners to Babylon. \q They will blow her away like chaff and leave her land empty. \q They will attack her from every side on the day of disaster.

decisions.choice: strangers ... winnow: a play on two words that sound alike
decisions.reason: The word for "strangers" (*zarim*) and the verb "winnow" (*zarah*) sound alike, so the foreigners who come against Babylon are pictured as winnowers. Winnowing tossed threshed grain into the wind, which carried the chaff away (15:7; Isaiah 41:16). The same letters could also be read "winnowers", which the play invites; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: empty her land: strip it of people and goods
decisions.reason: The verb means to empty out or lay waste, as a jar is emptied (19:7; Isaiah 24:1). The land will be left bare like a threshing floor after the wind has done its work.

decisions.choice: foreigners; blow her away like chaff
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "foreigners", the plain sense of the word. Readable explains winnowing as blowing chaff away, so that the picture is clear.

source.text: אֶֽל־יִדְרֹ֤ךְ הַדֹּרֵךְ֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְאֶל־יִתְעַ֖ל בְּסִרְיֹנ֑וֹ וְאַֽל־תַּחְמְלוּ֙ אֶל־בַּ֣חֻרֶ֔יהָ הַחֲרִ֖ימוּ כָּל־צְבָאָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Against [him who] bends let bend the [one] bending his bow, and against [him who] lifts himself in his armor; and do not spare her young men; devote to destruction all her army.

en.L: Against the one who bends [his bow] let the archer bend his bow, \q and against the one who rises up in his armor; \q do not spare her young men; \q devote all her army to destruction.
en.B: Let the archer bend his bow against her archer, \q against the one who stands up in his armor. \q Do not spare her young men; \q destroy her whole army completely.
en.R: Let the archers shoot at her archers \q and at her soldiers wearing armor. \q Do not spare her young men. \q Destroy her whole army, as given over to the LORD.

decisions.choice: against the one who bends: the attackers are to shoot down Babylon's archers and armored men
alternatives: Let not the archer bend his bow, nor rise up in his armor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew as pointed says "against" twice. Read that way, the line commands the attackers to aim their bows at Babylon's defenders. With a change of one vowel the same letters mean "let not", and the line would say "Let not the archer bend his bow, let him not rise up in his armor", that is, Babylon's soldiers will not even get to fight. The second half of the verse speaks to the attackers, which suits the first reading. The written text also repeats the verb "bend"; the reading tradition reads it once.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give over wholly to God by destroying it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for *cherem*, the destruction of an enemy as something devoted to God (Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 6:21). Babylon's army is to be destroyed without survivors (50:21, 26).

decisions.choice: [his bow]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object the first verb leaves out. Balanced and Readable say "her archer" and "her soldiers" to show whom the attackers aim at (m1).

decisions.choice: Destroy ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in Numbers to Ruth, Readable explains the verb of *cherem* rather than using "devote".

source.text: וְנָפְל֥וּ חֲלָלִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וּמְדֻקָּרִ֖ים בְּחוּצוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will fall slain in [the] land of [the] Chaldeans and pierced in her streets.

en.L: And they will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, \q and pierced through in her streets.
en.B: They will fall dead in the land of the Chaldeans, \q run through in her streets.
en.R: Her people will fall dead in the land of Babylonia. \q They will be stabbed to death in her streets.

decisions.choice: slain ... pierced through: killed by weapons
decisions.reason: The first word names those killed in battle; the second, those stabbed through with a sword or spear (37:10; Isaiah 13:15). The killing reaches into the city's own streets.

decisions.choice: Babylonia; Her people
decisions.reason: Readable says "Babylonia" for the land of the Chaldeans and names who falls, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

source.text: כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אַלְמָ֨ן יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וִֽיהוּדָה֙ מֵֽאֱלֹהָ֔יו מֵֽיְהוָ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת כִּ֤י אַרְצָם֙ מָלְאָ֣ה אָשָׁ֔ם מִקְּד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: For not widowed [is] Israel and Judah from his God, from Yahweh of hosts, for their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.

en.L: For Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God, \q of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q though their land is full of guilt \q against the Holy One of Israel.
en.B: For Israel and Judah have not been left widowed by their God, \q by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q though their land is filled with guilt \q against the Holy One of Israel.
en.R: Israel and Judah are not like widows whose husband is gone. \q Their God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, has not left them, \q even though their land is filled with sin \q against the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: widowed: left without a husband to protect them
decisions.reason: Israel is pictured as a wife and the LORD as her husband (3:14; 31:32; Isaiah 54:4-6). Though she is in exile, he has not died or left her; he will act for her against Babylon.

decisions.choice: though their land is full of guilt: most likely Israel's land, in spite of its sin
alternatives: for the land of the Chaldeans is full of guilt
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "for" or "though", and "their land" can mean the land of Israel and Judah or the land of the Chaldeans. Read as "though", the line says the LORD keeps faith with his people in spite of their sin. Read as "for", it gives the reason for Babylon's punishment: the Chaldeans' land is full of guilt against the Holy One. The words "their land" most naturally refer back to Israel and Judah, just named.

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel
decisions.reason: Isaiah's title for God (Isaiah 1:4), used in Jeremiah only in the oracle against Babylon (50:29; 51:5). Babylon's pride is an offense against Israel's holy God.

decisions.choice: like widows whose husband is gone ... has not left them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the widow (m1) in two sentences.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts".

source.text: נֻ֣סוּ׀מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֗ל וּמַלְּטוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ אַל־תִּדַּ֖מּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּי֩ עֵ֨ת נְקָמָ֥ה הִיא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה גְּמ֕וּל ה֥וּא מְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Flee from [the] midst of Babylon and save each his life; do not be silenced in her iniquity, for [it is the] time of vengeance for Yahweh; [the] recompense he [is] repaying to her.

en.L: Flee from the midst of Babylon, \q and save your lives, each one; \q do not be destroyed in her iniquity, \q for it is the time of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s vengeance; \q the recompense {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is paying back to her.
en.B: Flee from Babylon! \q Every one of you, run for your life! \q Do not be destroyed when she is punished for her guilt, \q for this is the time of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s vengeance; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is paying her back what she deserves.
en.R: Run away from Babylon! \q Everyone, run for your life! \q Do not die when she is punished for her sins. \q It is time for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to pay her back. \q He will give her what she deserves.

decisions.choice: be destroyed: be cut off, perish
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to be silent and so to be destroyed (8:14; 25:37; 47:5). Those who stay in Babylon will be caught up in her end.

decisions.choice: her iniquity: her guilt and the punishment it brings
decisions.reason: The word means wrongdoing and also the penalty that follows it (Genesis 4:13). Those who stay will share Babylon's punishment. The call to flee returns in verse 45 and 50:8.

decisions.choice: recompense: what she has earned
decisions.reason: The word means a deed's full return, good or bad (Isaiah 59:18). Babylon receives what her deeds deserve; verse 56 calls the LORD "a God of recompense".

decisions.choice: when she is punished for her guilt (Balanced); for her sins (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "in her iniquity" means (m2). Iniquity is "guilt" at Balanced and "sin" at Readable, as Isaiah does.

source.text: כּוֹס־זָהָ֤ב בָּבֶל֙ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁכֶּ֖רֶת כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ מִיֵּינָהּ֙ שָׁת֣וּ גוֹיִ֔ם עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִתְהֹלְל֥וּ גוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: A cup of gold [was] Babylon in [the] hand of Yahweh, making drunk all the earth; from her wine nations drank; therefore nations go mad.

en.L: Babylon [was] a cup of gold in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hand, \q making all the earth drunk; \q the nations drank of her wine; \q therefore the nations go mad.
en.B: Babylon was a golden cup in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hand, \q making the whole earth drunk; \q the nations drank her wine, \q and so the nations have gone mad.
en.R: Babylon was like a gold cup that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} held in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. \q She made the whole world drunk. \q The nations drank her wine, \q and so they acted as if they were crazy.

decisions.choice: a cup of gold in the LORD's hand: Babylon as the cup of God's wrath
decisions.reason: In 25:15-29 the LORD gives Jeremiah the cup of the wine of his wrath for the nations to drink, and the nations reel and go mad (25:16). Here Babylon herself is that cup: through her conquests God made the nations drink his judgment. The cup is gold because Babylon was rich and splendid. Revelation 17:4 and 18:3 take up the picture.

decisions.choice: go mad: act out of their minds
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 25:16 of the nations who drink the cup: they lose control like drunken people.

decisions.choice: was a cup: Babylon's past role, now ending
decisions.reason: There is no verb. Babylon has been God's cup; now (verse 8) the cup itself falls and breaks.

decisions.choice: like a gold cup that the LORD held
decisions.reason: Readable says "like" to mark the picture as a comparison, and "acted as if they were crazy" for the verb of madness, as in 25:16.

source.text: פִּתְאֹ֛ם נָפְלָ֥ה בָבֶ֖ל וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ עָלֶ֗יהָ קְח֤וּ צֳרִי֙ לְמַכְאוֹבָ֔הּ אוּלַ֖י תֵּרָפֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is broken; wail over her; take balm for her pain; perhaps she will be healed.

en.L: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered; \q wail over her! Take balm for her pain; \q perhaps she will be healed.
en.B: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered. \q Wail over her! Bring balm for her wound; \q perhaps she can be healed.
en.R: All of a sudden Babylon has fallen and is broken to pieces. \q Cry out in grief for her! Bring healing balm for her wound. \q Maybe she can be healed.

decisions.choice: has fallen: what is certain to happen told as if already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past tense, a way prophets announce a coming event as certain. The fall is sudden, like the fall of a cup from the hand (verse 7).

decisions.choice: take balm ... perhaps she will be healed: a mocking echo of 8:22 and 46:11
decisions.reason: Gilead's balm was a well-known medicine (8:22). In 46:11 Egypt is told to go up to Gilead for balm, in vain. Here those who see Babylon fall are told to try balm on her; the "perhaps" is ironic, and verse 9 says no cure works.

decisions.choice: her pain: her wound
decisions.reason: The word means pain, and here the wound that causes it (15:18; 30:15).

decisions.choice: Cry out in grief
decisions.reason: Readable says "Cry out in grief" for "Wail", the wording set in Isaiah.

source.text: רִפִּ֣ינוּ אֶת־בָּבֶל֙ וְלֹ֣א נִרְפָּ֔תָה עִזְב֕וּהָ וְנֵלֵ֖ךְ אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ כִּֽי־נָגַ֤ע אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִשְׁפָּטָ֔הּ וְנִשָּׂ֖א עַד־שְׁחָקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: We healed Babylon, and she was not healed; leave her, and let us go each to his land, for has reached to the heavens her judgment, and it is lifted up to [the] skies.

en.L: "We would have healed Babylon, but she was not healed. \q Leave her, and let us go, each to {{gender:their|his}} own land, \q for her judgment has reached to the heavens \q and is lifted up to the skies."
en.B: "We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. \q Leave her; let us go, each of us to our own land, \q for her judgment reaches up to the heavens; \q it rises as high as the clouds."
en.R: "We tried to make Babylon well, but she could not be healed. \q Let us leave her and go home, every one of us to our own country. \q Her punishment is as big as the sky. \q It reaches all the way to the clouds."

decisions.choice: we would have healed: we tried, but healing failed
decisions.reason: The verb describes an attempt that did not succeed. The speakers are those told in verse 8 to bring balm: probably foreigners living in Babylon, or her allies, who now give her up and go home. The written text and the text as read differ in the spelling of this verb, not in its sense.

decisions.choice: her judgment reaches to the heavens: her guilt and the sentence on it are beyond measure
decisions.reason: Judgment here is the sentence passed on Babylon, and the guilt that earned it. It reaches the sky because it is too great to be undone (compare Genesis 18:20-21; Ezra 9:6). Revelation 18:5 echoes the line.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the speakers of verse 9
decisions.reason: The poem quotes a group speaking in the first person, so the words take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside an oracle does in Isaiah. Literal's "each to their own land" has "his" as the gender alternative, since men and women speak; Balanced and Readable say "each of us to our own", which needs none.

source.text: הוֹצִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ בֹּ֚אוּ וּנְסַפְּרָ֣ה בְצִיּ֔וֹן אֶֽת־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh has brought out our vindications; come and let us recount in Zion the work of Yahweh our God.

en.L: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has brought out our vindication; \q come, and let us tell in Zion \q the work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has brought our vindication to light. \q Come, let us make known in Zion \q the work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."
en.R: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has shown that we were in the right. \q Come, let us tell the people in Zion \q what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has done."

decisions.choice: our vindication: the LORD's acts that show his people to be in the right
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of *tsedaqah*, "righteousness". The plural names acts of righteousness, here the LORD's acts that put his people in the right against their oppressor, as a judge does when he decides a case for the one wronged (Micah 7:9; Psalm 37:6). It is not a claim that the people had no sin (verse 5).

decisions.choice: come, let us tell: a new group of speakers, the people of Zion in exile
decisions.reason: After the foreigners of verse 9, the exiles of Israel and Judah speak. They want to go home and tell in Zion what the LORD has done, as 50:28 says.

decisions.choice: a new quotation
decisions.reason: The words of the exiles take their own double quotation marks. Readable says what vindication means in plain words.

source.text: הָבֵ֣רוּ הַחִצִּים֮ מִלְא֣וּ הַשְּׁלָטִים֒ הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ר֨וּחַ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י מָדַ֔י כִּֽי־עַל־בָּבֶ֥ל מְזִמָּת֖וֹ לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֑הּ כִּֽי־נִקְמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ הִ֔יא נִקְמַ֖ת הֵיכָלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Sharpen the arrows; fill the shields; Yahweh has stirred up [the] spirit of [the] kings of Media, for against Babylon his purpose [is] to destroy her; for [the] vengeance of Yahweh [is] it, [the] vengeance of his temple.

en.L: Sharpen the arrows; fill the quivers! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purpose concerning Babylon is to destroy her; \q for it is the vengeance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the vengeance for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple.
en.B: Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has roused the spirit of the Median kings, \q because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan is to destroy Babylon. \q This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s vengeance, \q vengeance for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple.
en.R: Sharpen your arrows! Fill your bags with arrows! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has moved the kings of the Medes to attack, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided to destroy Babylon. \q This is how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will pay Babylon back, \q because she destroyed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple.

decisions.choice: quivers: probably the cases that hold arrows; possibly shields
decisions.reason: The word is rare (2 Samuel 8:7; Ezekiel 27:11; Song 4:4). It is often taken as "shields", but "fill the shields" is a strange command, and beside "sharpen the arrows" it most likely means quivers, which are filled with arrows. If it means shields, the sense may be "take up the shields" or "fit the shields", that is, make ready for battle.

decisions.choice: the kings of the Medes: the rulers of Media and its allied peoples
decisions.reason: Media lay in the mountains east of Babylonia. Its kings had joined Babylon to destroy Assyria in the seventh century BC, but by the sixth century Media was part of the empire of Cyrus the Persian, and Medes were among the forces that took Babylon in 539 BC (Isaiah 13:17; Daniel 5:28-31). "Kings" may include the lesser kings under Media's rule (verse 28).

decisions.choice: the vengeance for his temple: for Babylon's burning of the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Babylon burned the LORD's house in 587 BC (52:13). As in 50:28, the destruction of Babylon is the LORD's answer to that act.

decisions.choice: moved ... to attack; because she destroyed his temple
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stirred up the spirit" and says what the vengeance for the temple is for (m3). It says "bags with arrows" for quivers.

source.text: אֶל־חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ־נֵ֗ס הַחֲזִ֨יקוּ֙ הַמִּשְׁמָ֔ר הָקִ֨ימוּ֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים הָכִ֖ינוּ הָאֹֽרְבִ֑ים כִּ֚י גַּם־זָמַ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה גַּם־עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Against [the] walls of Babylon lift up a signal flag; strengthen the watch; station watchmen; prepare the ambushes; for both has planned Yahweh, also he has done what he spoke concerning [the] inhabitants of Babylon.

en.L: Against the walls of Babylon raise a signal flag; \q strengthen the watch, station watchmen, \q prepare the ambushes! \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has both planned and done \q what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
en.B: Raise a signal flag against the walls of Babylon! \q Strengthen the guard, post the watchmen, \q set the ambushes! \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has planned it, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done it: \q what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said against the people of Babylon.
en.R: Raise a signal flag to attack the walls of Babylon! \q Put more guards on watch. Post the watchmen. \q Get men ready to hide and attack by surprise! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has planned what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do to the people of Babylon, \q and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done it.

decisions.choice: raise ... strengthen ... prepare: orders to the attackers to set the siege
decisions.reason: The commands most likely speak to the armies coming against Babylon: raise the flag that calls the troops, keep a close watch around the city so no one escapes, and set men in hiding to catch any who try. They could also be mocking orders to Babylon's defenders, who will strengthen the watch in vain. Either way, the second half says the outcome is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: signal flag: a banner raised on a pole to gather troops
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, the *nes* is a flag or banner raised on a height as a rallying sign (4:6; 50:2; 51:27).

decisions.choice: both planned and done: what the LORD intends, he carries out
decisions.reason: The two verbs together say that his purpose and his act are one (4:28; Lamentations 2:17). Babylon's fall is not chance but the fulfillment of his word.

decisions.choice: men ready to hide and attack by surprise
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ambushes" in plain words.

source.text: שֹׁכַנְתְּ֙ עַל־מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים רַבַּ֖ת אֽוֹצָרֹ֑ת בָּ֥א קִצֵּ֖ךְ אַמַּ֥ת בִּצְעֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [You who] dwell on many waters, great of treasures, has come your end, [the] cubit of your cutting off.

en.L: You who dwell by many waters, \q rich in treasures, \q your end has come, the cubit of your cutting off.
en.B: You who live beside many waters, \q you with your wealth of treasures, \q your end has come; the thread of your life is measured to be cut.
en.R: You live beside many rivers and canals, \q and you have great treasures. \q But your end has come. Your life will be cut off like thread cut from a loom.

decisions.choice: many waters: the Euphrates and the canals of Babylon
decisions.reason: Babylon stood on the Euphrates, and a network of canals watered its fields and protected the city (Psalm 137:1). The waters that made it rich and safe could not save it (verse 36). Revelation 17:1 takes up the phrase.

decisions.choice: the cubit of your cutting off: the length of your thread has been measured, and it is cut
alternatives: the measure of your unjust gain is full
decisions.reason: A cubit was a measure of length, also used of cloth. The second word comes from a verb meaning to cut off, used of a weaver cutting the finished cloth from the loom (Isaiah 38:12). The sense is that Babylon's life has reached its measured length and is cut off. The same noun often means unjust gain, and the line could mean "the measure of your plunder is full", that is, the limit of your greed has been reached.

decisions.choice: you who dwell: an old spelling in the written text
decisions.reason: The written text spells the verb with an older ending; the text as read has the usual form. The meaning is the same (compare 22:23).

decisions.choice: the thread of your life is measured to be cut (Balanced); like thread cut from a loom (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "cubit". Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m2); they use no measure, since "cubit" here is part of a figure of speech, not a measurement.

source.text: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־מִלֵּאתִ֤יךְ אָדָם֙ כַּיֶּ֔לֶק וְעָנ֥וּ עָלַ֖יִךְ הֵידָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Has sworn Yahweh of hosts by his soul: surely I will fill you [with] men like locusts, and they will raise over you a shout.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}: \q Surely I will fill you with men like locusts, \q and they will raise over you a shout [of victory].
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}: \q I will fill you with men, as many as locusts, \q and they will shout in triumph over you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made a promise and sworn by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own life: \q I will fill your streets with enemy soldiers, as many as locusts, \q and they will shout over you because they have won.

decisions.choice: has sworn by himself: the strongest oath possible
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "by his soul", that is, by his own life. Since there is none greater, God swears by himself (22:5; 49:13; Genesis 22:16; Amos 6:8; Hebrews 6:13).

decisions.choice: surely: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: The words "for if" introduce the content of an oath and mean "surely" (Numbers 14:28).

decisions.choice: like locusts ... a shout: an army past counting, shouting over its prey
decisions.reason: Locust swarms stood for numbers beyond counting (46:23; Judges 6:5). The shout is the cry of grape treaders, here a victory shout (25:30; 48:33).

decisions.choice: [of victory] (L); in triumph (B); because they have won (R)
decisions.reason: The word names a loud rhythmic shout; in this setting it is a shout over the defeated, so Literal supplies "[of victory]" and Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנָת֖וֹ נָטָ֥ה שָׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: [He is the] maker of [the] earth by his power, establisher of [the] world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out [the] heavens.

en.L: [He is] the maker of the earth by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, \q who established the world by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out the heavens.
en.B: It is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who made the earth by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, \q who set the world firm by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding spread out the heavens.
en.R: God made the earth by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power. \q He set the world firmly in place by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom. \q He used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} understanding to spread out the sky.

decisions.choice: verses 15-19 repeat 10:12-16, here word for word
decisions.reason: The hymn to the LORD as Creator in 10:12-16 returns here almost unchanged, and this verse matches 10:12 exactly. In chapter 10 it sets the living God against idols; here it gives the reason Babylon, with all her gods, cannot stand against him. The wording of 10:12-16 is kept wherever the Hebrew is the same, and each difference is noted.

decisions.choice: maker ... establisher: the LORD described by what he did
decisions.reason: As in 10:12. The verse begins with words describing the LORD who has just sworn by himself (verse 14).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: As in 10:12, Readable names the subject.

source.text: לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֨יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּ֥עַל נְשִׂאִ֖ים מִקְצֵה־אָ֑רֶץ בְּרָקִ֤ים לַמָּטָר֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיֹּ֥צֵא ר֖וּחַ מֵאֹצְרֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: At [the] sound of his giving, a roar of waters in the heavens, and he makes go up clouds from [the] end of earth; lightnings for the rain he makes, and he brings out wind from his storehouses.

en.L: At the sound of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} giving forth [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice], [there is] a roar of waters in the heavens, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes clouds rise from the end of the earth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes lightning for the rain \q and brings out wind from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} storehouses.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raises the clouds from the far edges of the earth. \q He makes lightning flash with the rain \q and brings the wind out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} storehouses.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thunders, the waters in the sky roar. \q He makes clouds rise up from far away at the edge of the world. \q He sends lightning with the rain. \q He brings out the wind from the places where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps it.

decisions.choice: as 10:13, with small differences of spelling only
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 10:13. Two verbs are written in shorter forms, and "the earth" lacks the article; none of this changes the sense, so the wording of 10:13 is kept.

decisions.choice: at the sound of his giving: when he thunders
decisions.reason: As in 10:13, to "give one's voice" is to speak out, and of God it means thunder (Psalm 18:14).

decisions.choice: a roar of waters in the heavens: the rain held above the sky
decisions.reason: As in 10:13 (Genesis 1:7; Psalm 148:4). The phrase also answers verse 13: Babylon dwells on many waters, but the LORD rules all the waters above and below.

decisions.choice: When he thunders
decisions.reason: As in 10:13, Balanced and Readable say what "giving his voice" means.

source.text: נִבְעַ֤ר כָּל־אָדָם֙ מִדַּ֔עַת הֹבִ֥ישׁ כָּל־צֹרֵ֖ף מִפָּ֑סֶל כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר נִסְכּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־ר֥וּחַ בָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Is stupid every man without knowledge; is put to shame every smith by [the] idol, for a lie [is] his cast image, and no breath [is] in them.

en.L: Every {{gender:human|man}} is stupid, without knowledge; \q every smith is put to shame by [his] idol, \q for his cast image [is] a lie, and [there is] no breath in them.
en.B: Everyone proves senseless and ignorant; \q every goldsmith is shamed by his idol, \q for the images he casts are a fraud, with no breath in them.
en.R: Everyone who makes idols is stupid and knows nothing. \q Every goldsmith will be ashamed of the idol he made. \q His metal statues are fakes, and there is no life in them.

decisions.choice: as 10:14, with one word spelled differently
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 10:14; "smith" is spelled without one letter, with no change of sense. The wording of 10:14 is kept. In this chapter the idols are Babylon's own (verses 44, 47, 52).

decisions.choice: every human is stupid, without knowledge: people shown up as senseless
decisions.reason: As in 10:14. Beside the wisdom of God who made the world (verse 15), those who trust in idols are shown to know nothing.

decisions.choice: a lie ... no breath: a false god with no life
decisions.reason: As in 10:14. The image pretends to be a god and has no breath of life.

decisions.choice: Everyone who makes idols
decisions.reason: As in 10:14, Readable narrows "every person" to those who make idols. It is a stretch from the general words, which could also mean that every person is senseless beside God's wisdom.

source.text: הֶ֣בֶל הֵ֔מָּה מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה תַּעְתֻּעִ֑ים בְּעֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Futility [are] they, a work of mockeries; at [the] time of their punishment they will perish.

en.L: They [are] futility, a work of mockery; \q at the time of their punishment they will perish.
en.B: They are empty breath, a work to be laughed at; \q when the time comes to punish them, they will perish.
en.R: Idols are worthless, something to laugh at. \q When God comes to punish them, they will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: the same as 10:15
decisions.reason: The Hebrew matches 10:15 exactly, and its wording is kept.

decisions.choice: futility ... a work of mockery
decisions.reason: As in 10:15: the idols are empty breath, things that deceive and deserve to be laughed at. The word for "mockery" appears only here and in 10:15.

decisions.choice: the time of their punishment: when God comes to deal with them
decisions.reason: As in 10:15. Verses 44, 47 and 52 say when that time comes for Babylon's idols.

decisions.choice: Idols ... God comes
decisions.reason: As in 10:15.

source.text: לֹֽא־כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲק֗וֹב כִּֽי־יוֹצֵ֤ר הַכֹּל֙ ה֔וּא וְשֵׁ֖בֶט נַחֲלָת֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not like these [is the] portion of Jacob, for [the] former of the all he [is], and [the] tribe of his inheritance; Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.

en.L: Not like these [is] the portion of Jacob, for the one who formed all things [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, \q and [also] the tribe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: The God who is Jacob's portion is not like these, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who formed all things, \q including the tribe {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: But the God who belongs to Jacob's people is not like these idols, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made everything there is. \q He also made the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own. \q His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: as 10:16, but without the word "Israel"
alternatives: and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance, with Israel understood from 10:16
decisions.reason: In 10:16 the line reads "and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance". Here "Israel" is lacking, and the line joins on to what comes before: the LORD formed all things, and the tribe he holds as his own among them. It may also be read with "Israel" understood from 10:16; the sense is close either way. "Jacob" is also spelled more fully here. Otherwise the wording of 10:16 is kept.

decisions.choice: the portion of Jacob: God himself is the share that belongs to his people
decisions.reason: As in 10:16 (Deuteronomy 32:9; Psalm 16:5; Lamentations 3:24).

decisions.choice: the tribe of his inheritance: the people God holds as his own
decisions.reason: As in 10:16 (Psalm 74:2). After the hymn, the poem turns back to Babylon (verse 20).

decisions.choice: [also] (L); including (B); He also made (R)
decisions.reason: Without "Israel", the line is joined to "the one who formed all things" (m1). Literal brackets the joining word; Balanced and Readable say "including" and "also". Balanced and Readable keep the rest of the wording of 10:16, with "Armies" for "hosts".

source.text: מַפֵּץ־אַתָּ֣ה לִ֔י כְּלֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִשְׁחַתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: A war club [are] you to me, weapons of war; and I shatter with you nations, and I destroy with you kingdoms.

en.L: You [are] my war club, [my] weapon of war; \q and with you I shatter nations, \q and with you I destroy kingdoms.
en.B: You are my war club, my weapon of war: \q with you I shatter nations; \q with you I destroy kingdoms.
en.R: You are my war club, the weapon I use in battle. \q With you I smash nations. \q With you I destroy kingdoms.

decisions.choice: war club ... I shatter: a play on one root
decisions.reason: The word *mappets* means a club or hammer for smashing, from the root of the verb "shatter" that follows nine times in verses 20-23; the tenth verb is "destroy". The repetition is the point: whatever the club strikes is broken. Babylon was called "the hammer of the whole earth" in 50:23, with a different word.

decisions.choice: you: most likely Babylon, the LORD's weapon against the nations
alternatives: the conqueror who will destroy Babylon
decisions.reason: The poem does not name the "you". Babylon fits best: God used her to break the nations (25:9; 27:6; 50:23), and verse 24 turns to repay her. Others read "you" as the coming conqueror, Cyrus, or as Israel, through whom God will break Babylon. The verbs can describe what God has done again and again or what he will do; the present tense keeps both open.

decisions.choice: with you I shatter (L, B); With you I smash (R): the same words each time
decisions.reason: The phrase is kept the same through all ten lines of verses 20-23 at each level, so that the hammer blows can be heard. Literal supplies "[my]".

source.text: וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ ס֖וּס וְרֹֽכְב֑וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ רֶ֖כֶב וְרֹכְבֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I shatter with you horse and its rider, and I shatter with you chariot and its rider.

en.L: and with you I shatter horse and its rider, \q and with you I shatter chariot and its rider;
en.B: with you I shatter horse and rider; \q with you I shatter chariot and driver;
en.R: With you I smash horses and their riders. \q With you I smash chariots and their drivers.

decisions.choice: chariot and its rider: the war chariot and the man who drives it
decisions.reason: The same word "rider" is used for one on horseback and one in a chariot. Horses and chariots were the strength of an ancient army (Exodus 15:1, 21; Psalm 20:8).

decisions.choice: driver
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "driver" for the one who rides in a chariot. The repeated phrase stays as in verse 20.

source.text: וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ זָקֵ֣ן וָנָ֑עַר וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ בָּח֖וּר וּבְתוּלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I shatter with you man and woman, and I shatter with you old [man] and youth, and I shatter with you young man and young woman.

en.L: and with you I shatter man and woman, \q and with you I shatter old and young, \q and with you I shatter young man and young woman;
en.B: with you I shatter man and woman; \q with you I shatter old and young; \q with you I shatter young man and young woman;
en.R: With you I smash men and women. \q With you I smash old people and young people. \q With you I smash young men and young women.

decisions.choice: pairs that take in everyone
decisions.reason: The pairs, man and woman, old and young, young man and young woman, are a way of saying "all people" (compare 6:11). The word for "young" in the second pair often means a boy or youth.

decisions.choice: the repeated phrase kept
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

source.text: וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ רֹעֶ֣ה וְעֶדְר֔וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ אִכָּ֣ר וְצִמְדּ֑וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ פַּח֖וֹת וּסְגָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I shatter with you shepherd and his flock, and I shatter with you farmer and his team, and I shatter with you governors and officials.

en.L: and with you I shatter shepherd and his flock, \q and with you I shatter farmer and his team, \q and with you I shatter governors and officials.
en.B: with you I shatter shepherd and flock; \q with you I shatter farmer and team of oxen; \q with you I shatter governors and officials.
en.R: With you I smash shepherds and their flocks. \q With you I smash farmers and the oxen that pull their plows. \q With you I smash governors and officials.

decisions.choice: his team: the pair of oxen yoked to the plow
decisions.reason: The word means a pair, a yoke of oxen working together (1 Samuel 11:7; 1 Kings 19:19).

decisions.choice: governors and officials: titles of rulers in the empires of the day
decisions.reason: Both words came into Hebrew from the language of Assyria and Babylon. They name provincial governors and lesser officials (verses 28, 57; Isaiah 41:25; Ezekiel 23:6). The list runs from the herdsman to the rulers: no one is beyond the club's reach.

decisions.choice: team of oxen (B); the oxen that pull their plows (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the team is (m1).

source.text: וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל וּלְכֹ֣ל׀יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֗ים אֵ֧ת כָּל־רָעָתָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֥וּ בְצִיּ֖וֹן לְעֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will repay to Babylon and to all [the] inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they did in Zion before your eyes, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea \q for all their evil that they have done in Zion before your eyes, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: But I will repay Babylon and all who live in Chaldea \q for all the evil they have done in Zion before your eyes, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: But I will pay back Babylon and all the people of Babylonia \q for all the evil they did in Jerusalem while you watched, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: and I will repay: the turn from Babylon's past use to its punishment
decisions.reason: After the ten blows of verses 20-23, the LORD declares that the weapon he used will itself be repaid. The verb is the one used in verses 6 and 56.

decisions.choice: before your eyes: the evil done in Zion while you, the exiles, watched
alternatives: I will repay them before your eyes
decisions.reason: The "your" is plural and speaks to the people of Judah. The phrase most naturally goes with what comes just before it, the evil done in Zion, which they saw with their own eyes. It could also go with the repaying: they will see Babylon punished (50:28).

decisions.choice: Jerusalem; Babylonia; while you watched
decisions.reason: Readable says "Jerusalem" for Zion and "Babylonia" for Chaldea, and "while you watched" for "before your eyes" (m2).

source.text: הִנְנִ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ הַ֤ר הַמַּשְׁחִית֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה הַמַּשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנָטִ֨יתִי אֶת־יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וְגִלְגַּלְתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן־הַסְּלָעִ֔ים וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְהַ֥ר שְׂרֵפָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Here I [am] against you, mountain of the destroyer, declares Yahweh, the [one] destroying all the earth; and I will stretch out my hand against you and roll you from the crags and make you a mountain of burning.

en.L: Look, I am against you, O destroying mountain, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q you who destroy all the earth; \q and I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and roll you down from the crags, \q and make you a burned mountain.
en.B: I am against you, destroying mountain, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q you who destroy the whole earth. \q I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and roll you down from the cliffs, \q and make you a burned-out mountain.
en.R: Babylon, you are like a mountain that destroys the whole earth. \q But now I am against you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will reach out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and roll you down from the cliffs. \q I will make you a mountain burned to ashes.

decisions.choice: destroying mountain: Babylon as a towering power that ruins the earth
decisions.reason: Babylon stood on a flat plain, so the mountain is a picture of its height and power, the empire that loomed over the nations (compare Daniel 2:35). The word "destroying" is the one used in verse 1 of the wind God sends: the destroyer is now destroyed. The same phrase names a hill near Jerusalem where Solomon built shrines to foreign gods (2 Kings 23:13), but there is no clear link here.

decisions.choice: rolled from the crags ... a burned mountain: a peak toppled and burned out
decisions.reason: The picture may be of a mountain set on fire and left a heap of burned rock, or of a fortress on the heights thrown down and burned. Either way, Babylon will be left lifeless, good for nothing (verse 26; compare Revelation 8:8).

decisions.choice: stretch out my hand against you: act in judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the LORD striking a people (6:12; 15:6; Exodus 7:5).

decisions.choice: Babylon, you are like a mountain
decisions.reason: Readable names Babylon and says "like" to show that the mountain is a picture (m1). It puts "says the LORD" in the second sentence so the first can explain the picture.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־יִקְח֤וּ מִמְּךָ֙ אֶ֣בֶן לְפִנָּ֔ה וְאֶ֖בֶן לְמֽוֹסָד֑וֹת כִּֽי־שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֛ם תִּֽהְיֶ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they will take from you a stone for a corner, or a stone for foundations; for desolations of forever you will be, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And they will not take from you a stone for a corner \q or a stone for foundations, \q for you will be a desolation forever, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: No one will take a cornerstone from you, \q or any stone for a foundation, \q for you will be a desolation forever, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: No one will take a single stone from you \q to build the corner or the foundation of a house. \q You will be an empty ruin forever, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a stone for a corner or for foundations: the best stones, used to start a building
decisions.reason: The cornerstone and foundation stones had to be large and sound (Isaiah 28:16; Psalm 118:22). A burned mountain would yield no stone good enough even for that: nothing in Babylon will be fit to build again.

decisions.choice: a desolation forever: a ruin that will last
decisions.reason: The plural "desolations" stresses how complete the ruin is. Verse 62 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: to build the corner or the foundation of a house
decisions.reason: Readable says what the stones are used for (m1).

source.text: שְׂאוּ־נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ תִּקְע֨וּ שׁוֹפָ֤ר בַּגּוֹיִם֙ קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם הַשְׁמִ֧יעוּ עָלֶ֛יהָ מַמְלְכ֥וֹת אֲרָרַ֖ט מִנִּ֣י וְאַשְׁכְּנָ֑ז פִּקְד֤וּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ טִפְסָ֔ר הַֽעֲלוּ־ס֖וּס כְּיֶ֥לֶק סָמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Lift up a signal flag in the land; blow a horn among [the] nations; consecrate against her nations; summon against her [the] kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz; appoint against her a marshal; bring up horse like bristling locusts.

en.L: Raise a signal flag in the land; blow the trumpet among the nations; consecrate nations against her; \q summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz; \q appoint a marshal against her; \q bring up horses like bristling locusts.
en.B: Raise a signal flag in the land! Sound the ram's horn among the nations! Set apart nations for holy war against her; \q summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz! \q Appoint a commander against her; \q send up horses like a swarm of bristling locusts!
en.R: Raise a signal flag in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Get the nations ready to fight against Babylon. \q Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz to attack her. \q Choose a commander to lead the attack. \q Send so many horses that they look like a swarm of locusts.

decisions.choice: Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz: peoples of the mountains north of Babylon
decisions.reason: Ararat is the kingdom of Urartu, in the mountains of what is now Armenia and eastern Turkey (Genesis 8:4; 2 Kings 19:37). Minni is the land of the Manneans, south of Lake Urmia. Ashkenaz is usually linked with the Scythians, horsemen of the north (Genesis 10:3). In the sixth century BC these lands were under the rule of the Medes (verse 28), who would bring them against Babylon.

decisions.choice: consecrate: prepare for war with religious rites
decisions.reason: War was begun with sacrifices and acts that set the soldiers apart, so the verb "make holy" came to mean "prepare for battle" (6:4; 22:7; Joel 4:9).

decisions.choice: marshal: an officer who musters troops
decisions.reason: The word, borrowed from the language of Babylon, names an official, here one who calls up and arranges an army. It appears only here and in Nahum 3:17.

decisions.choice: bristling locusts: locusts at a stage when their wings stand up stiff
decisions.reason: The word for "bristling" is used only here and may describe young locusts whose wings are still in stiff sheaths, or the rough hair of the horses' manes. Either way, the cavalry comes like a swarm (verse 14).

decisions.choice: ram's horn (B); Prepare the nations for holy war (B); commander (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "ram's horn" for the *shofar*, as Isaiah does. Balanced and Readable say what "consecrate" means here (m2) and use "commander" for the marshal.

source.text: קַדְּשׁ֨וּ עָלֶ֤יהָ גוֹיִם֙ אֶת־מַלְכֵ֣י מָדַ֔י אֶת־פַּחוֹתֶ֖יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־סְגָנֶ֑יהָ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Consecrate against her nations, [the] kings of Media, her governors and all her officials and all [the] land of his dominion.

en.L: Consecrate nations against her, the kings of the Medes, \q their governors and all their officials, \q and all the land of their dominion.
en.B: Set apart nations for holy war against her: the kings of the Medes, \q with their governors and all their officials, \q and every land they rule.
en.R: Get the nations ready to fight against Babylon: the kings of the Medes, \q together with their governors and officials, \q and all the lands under their rule.

decisions.choice: her governors ... his dominion: the rulers and lands under Media
decisions.reason: The pronouns shift: "her" refers to Media as a land, and "his" to its king, or to each king. The sense is the whole Median empire with all its subject peoples.

decisions.choice: governors and officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 23. Media's governors and officials ruled the lands named in verse 27.

decisions.choice: their governors ... their dominion
decisions.reason: English uses "their" for the shifting pronouns (m1), since they all point to the Medes and their kings.

source.text: וַתִּרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ וַתָּחֹ֑ל כִּ֣י קָ֤מָה עַל־בָּבֶל֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה לָשׂ֞וּם אֶת־אֶ֧רֶץ בָּבֶ֛ל לְשַׁמָּ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And quakes the land and writhes, for stand against Babylon [the] plans of Yahweh to make [the] land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.

en.L: And the land quakes and writhes, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s plans against Babylon stand, \q to make the land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.
en.B: The land trembles and writhes in pain, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s plans against Babylon stand firm: \q to make the land of Babylon a wasteland where no one lives.
en.R: The land shakes and twists in pain, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned against Babylon. \q He will make the land of Babylon an empty wasteland where no one lives.

decisions.choice: writhes: twists in pain, as in childbirth
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a woman in labor (4:31) and of the earth shaking at God's coming (Psalm 97:4). The land of Babylon shakes at what is coming.

decisions.choice: stand: are carried out and cannot be changed
decisions.reason: A plan that "stands" holds firm and comes to pass (44:28-29; Isaiah 14:24; 46:10).

decisions.choice: will do what he planned
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what it means for a plan to stand (m2).

source.text: חָדְלוּ֩ גִבּוֹרֵ֨י בָבֶ֜ל לְהִלָּחֵ֗ם יָֽשְׁבוּ֙ בַּמְּצָד֔וֹת נָשְׁתָ֥ה גְבוּרָתָ֖ם הָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים הִצִּ֥יתוּ מִשְׁכְּנֹתֶ֖יהָ נִשְׁבְּר֥וּ בְרִיחֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Cease [the] warriors of Babylon to fight; they sit in the strongholds; dried up [is] their strength; they have become women; they have set on fire her dwellings; broken [are] her bars.

en.L: The warriors of Babylon have ceased to fight; they sit in the strongholds; \q their strength has dried up; they have become women; \q her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.
en.B: Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they stay in their strongholds. \q Their strength is gone; they have become like women. \q Her houses are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.
en.R: Babylon's soldiers have stopped fighting. They stay inside their forts. \q Their strength is gone. They have lost all their courage. \q Her houses are burning. The bars that lock her gates are broken.

decisions.choice: they have become women: they have lost their nerve for battle
decisions.reason: In the language of ancient war, to say that soldiers "become women" meant that they had lost the strength and courage to fight and had become helpless (50:37; Isaiah 19:16; Nahum 3:13). The saying reflects the warfare of the time, in which women did not fight; it describes fear, not a judgment on women.

decisions.choice: the strongholds: the fortresses where they shelter
decisions.reason: The warriors do not go out to fight but stay behind their walls, which do not save them.

decisions.choice: her bars: the bars that lock the city gates
decisions.reason: Gates were closed with heavy bars of wood or bronze (49:31; Lamentations 2:9). Broken bars mean the city lies open.

decisions.choice: like women (B); They have lost all their courage (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "like" to mark the comparison; Readable says what the idiom means (m1). Balanced and Readable say "the bars of her gates" to make the picture clear.

source.text: רָ֤ץ לִקְרַאת־רָץ֙ יָר֔וּץ וּמַגִּ֖יד לִקְרַ֣את מַגִּ֑יד לְהַגִּיד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל כִּֽי־נִלְכְּדָ֥ה עִיר֖וֹ מִקָּצֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Runner to meet runner runs, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell [the] king of Babylon that has been captured his city from [the] end.

en.L: Runner runs to meet runner, \q and messenger to meet messenger, \q to tell the king of Babylon \q that his city has been captured from end [to end].
en.B: One runner runs to meet another, \q one messenger to meet the next, \q to tell the king of Babylon \q that his city has been taken from end to end.
en.R: One runner after another hurries to the king of Babylon. \q One messenger after another comes with news. \q They tell the king \q that his whole city has been captured.

decisions.choice: runner to meet runner: messengers coming one after another from every part of the city
decisions.reason: Kings received news by runners (2 Samuel 18:19-27). Here they meet one another on the way, each bringing word from a different quarter, until the king learns that the whole city has fallen.

decisions.choice: from end to end: from every side, the whole city
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from the end", meaning from its outer edge, on every side (50:26).

decisions.choice: from end [to end]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words English needs for the phrase (m2).

source.text: וְהַמַּעְבָּר֣וֹת נִתְפָּ֔שׂוּ וְאֶת־הָאֲגַמִּ֖ים שָׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֑שׁ וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה נִבְהָֽלוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the fords have been seized, and the reed marshes they have burned with fire, and the men of war are terrified.

en.L: And the fords have been seized, \q and the reed marshes they have burned with fire, \q and the men of war are terrified.
en.B: The river crossings are seized, \q the marshes of reeds are set on fire, \q and the soldiers are in panic.
en.R: The enemy has taken the places where people cross the river. \q They have set fire to the reeds in the marshes. \q Babylon's soldiers are terrified.

decisions.choice: the fords: the river crossings
decisions.reason: The word names places where a river can be crossed (Judges 3:28; 12:5). Once they are held, no help can come and no one can escape.

decisions.choice: the reed marshes burned: the cover of the city's waters destroyed
decisions.reason: The word usually means pools or marshes thick with reeds (Exodus 7:19; Isaiah 35:7). Burning them may mean burning the reeds that grew along Babylon's waters and gave cover or defense. "Burned" is a vivid way to say that the city's water defenses are lost.

decisions.choice: The enemy has taken
decisions.reason: Readable names who seizes the fords, which the passive verb leaves unstated.

source.text: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּת־בָּבֶ֕ל כְּגֹ֖רֶן עֵ֣ת הִדְרִיכָ֑הּ ע֣וֹד מְעַ֔ט וּבָ֥אָה עֵֽת־הַקָּצִ֖יר לָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: [The] daughter of Babylon [is] like a threshing floor [at the] time of trampling her; yet a little, and will come [the] time of the harvest for her.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: \q The daughter of Babylon [is] like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden; \q yet a little while, \q and the time of harvest will come for her.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: \q Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is stamped down; \q in a little while \q the time of her harvest will come.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: \q The city of Babylon is like a threshing floor that is being stamped hard and flat. \q Very soon \q it will be time to harvest her.

decisions.choice: a threshing floor at the time it is trodden: ready for the grain to be beaten
decisions.reason: A threshing floor was a flat place of hard earth or rock. Before harvest it was stamped down to make it smooth and firm; then the cut grain was spread on it and beaten (Isaiah 21:10; Micah 4:12-13). Babylon is being made ready for the threshing.

decisions.choice: the time of harvest: the time of judgment
decisions.reason: Harvest is a common picture of God's judgment on a people (Joel 4:13; Isaiah 17:5; Revelation 14:15).

decisions.choice: the daughter of Babylon: Babylon pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: As "Daughter Zion" is Jerusalem and its people, "Daughter Babylon" is the city personified (50:42; Isaiah 47:1).

decisions.choice: The city of Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Daughter Babylon" as the city, as Isaiah's terms list says to do.

source.text: אֲכָלַ֣נִי הֲמָמַ֗נִי נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶל֒ הִצִּיגַ֨נִי֙ כְּלִ֣י רִ֔יק בְּלָעַ֨נִי֙ כַּתַּנִּ֔ין מִלָּ֥א כְרֵשׂ֖וֹ מֵֽעֲדָנָ֑י הֱדִיחָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: He devoured me, he crushed me, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; he set me down [as] an empty vessel; he swallowed me like the sea monster; he filled his belly with my delicacies; he rinsed me out.

en.L: "He has devoured me, he has crushed me, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; \q he has set me down [like] an empty vessel; \q he has swallowed me like the sea monster; \q he has filled his belly with my delicacies; \q he has rinsed me out."
en.B: "Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has devoured me and crushed me; \q he has left me standing like an empty jar. \q He has swallowed me like a sea monster, \q filled his belly with my good things, \q and spewed me out."
en.R: "Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon has eaten me up. He has crushed me. \q He left me empty, like a jar with nothing in it. \q He swallowed me like a great sea monster. \q He filled his stomach with my best things. \q Then he spit me out."

decisions.choice: me: Zion, speaking as a woman wronged by Babylon
decisions.reason: The speaker is named in verse 35: the people of Zion, Jerusalem. The city speaks of herself as one person, as in Lamentations 1:12-22. The LORD answers her in verse 36.

decisions.choice: me: the text as read; the written text says "us"
decisions.reason: In the written text the verbs end "us": he devoured us, crushed us, set us down, swallowed us, rinsed us out. The text as read changes each to "me", to match "my delicacies" and verse 35, where Zion speaks as one. Both mean the same people.

decisions.choice: the sea monster ... rinsed me out: the dragon that swallows its prey whole
decisions.reason: The word names a great sea creature or dragon (Genesis 1:21; Isaiah 27:1). Babylon has swallowed Jerusalem as such a beast swallows its prey and spits out what is left. The last verb means to rinse or wash out, here of a vessel emptied or a mouth spitting out. Verse 44 answers: Bel will be made to give back what he swallowed.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name used in this verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here spells the king's name with an "r", as in most of Jeremiah. It is the same king as Nebuchadnezzar (27:6).

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for Zion's words, closing at the end of verse 35
decisions.reason: Zion's complaint is speech quoted inside the oracle, so it takes double quotation marks, with "the inhabitant of Zion will say" in verse 35 outside them. Balanced and Readable put the king's name first, as English needs a subject at the start.

source.text: חֲמָסִ֤י וּשְׁאֵרִי֙ עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל תֹּאמַ֖ר יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן וְדָמִי֙ אֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֔ים תֹּאמַ֖ר יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: My violence and my flesh [be] on Babylon, will say [the] inhabitant of Zion; and my blood [be] on [the] inhabitants of Chaldea, will say Jerusalem.

en.L: "The violence done to me and to my flesh [be] on Babylon," \q the inhabitant of Zion will say; \q "and my blood [be] on the inhabitants of Chaldea," \q Jerusalem will say.
en.B: "May the violence done to me and to my flesh fall on Babylon," \q the people of Zion will say. \q "May my blood be on those who live in Chaldea," \q Jerusalem will say.
en.R: The people of Zion will say, \q "May Babylon suffer the cruel things she did to us." \q The people of Jerusalem will say, \q "Babylon killed our people. May she pay for it."

decisions.choice: the violence done to me ... my blood be on: let the guilt and its punishment fall on them
decisions.reason: "Violence done to me" means the wrong done to me (Genesis 16:5). To say "my blood be on" someone is to call for him to answer for the bloodshed (26:15; 2 Samuel 1:16; Matthew 27:25). Zion asks God to bring on Babylon what she suffered.

decisions.choice: my flesh: my own body, or my own people
decisions.reason: The word means flesh, and can also mean one's own kin (Leviticus 18:6). It may mean Zion's own body torn by Babylon, or her people killed.

decisions.choice: the inhabitant of Zion: Zion's people, spoken of as one woman
decisions.reason: The form is singular and feminine, the population pictured as a woman, like "Daughter Zion".

decisions.choice: the violence done to me (L, B); May ... (B, R)
decisions.reason: English says whose violence is meant and makes the wish clear with "[be]" at Literal and "May" at Balanced and Readable. Readable says "us" and "our people" for the city's people and puts the speaker first.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי־רָב֙ אֶת־רִיבֵ֔ךְ וְנִקַּמְתִּ֖י אֶת־נִקְמָתֵ֑ךְ וְהַחֲרַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־יַמָּ֔הּ וְהֹבַשְׁתִּ֖י אֶת־מְקוֹרָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: Here I [am] pleading your case, and I will avenge your vengeance; and I will dry up her sea and make dry her spring.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Look, I will plead your case \q and take vengeance for you; \q and I will dry up her sea \q and make her spring dry.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q I will plead your case \q and avenge you. \q I will dry up her sea \q and leave her spring dry.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to Jerusalem: \q I will stand up for you in court. \q I will pay Babylon back for what she did to you. \q I will dry up her sea. \q I will make her springs run dry.

decisions.choice: plead your case: take up your cause as in a court of law
decisions.reason: The words picture a lawsuit in which the LORD speaks for the one wronged and wins her case (50:34; Micah 7:9; Lamentations 3:58). "Your" is feminine singular, Zion who has just spoken.

decisions.choice: her sea ... her spring: the waters that made Babylon great
decisions.reason: Babylon's "sea" is the Euphrates with its canals and marshes, the "many waters" of verse 13 (Isaiah 21:1). Drying them up takes away her wealth and defense (50:38; Isaiah 44:27).

decisions.choice: to Jerusalem; stand up for you in court
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the LORD speaks to and explains "plead your case" (m1).

source.text: וְהָיְתָה֩ בָבֶ֨ל׀לְגַלִּ֧ים׀מְעוֹן־תַּנִּ֛ים שַׁמָּ֥ה וּשְׁרֵקָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will become Babylon heaps, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.

en.L: And Babylon will become heaps, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.
en.B: Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, a horror and an object of scorn, where no one lives.
en.R: Babylon will become a pile of ruins where jackals live, a horror and something people mock, a place where no one lives.

decisions.choice: heaps, a haunt of jackals: a city turned to rubble where wild animals live
decisions.reason: As in 9:10 and 10:22, which say the same of Jerusalem: "heaps" are piles of stones from fallen buildings, and jackals make their dens in ruins far from people (49:33; Isaiah 13:22). What Babylon did to Jerusalem is done to Babylon.

decisions.choice: a horror and a hissing: a ruin that makes passers-by gasp and whistle
decisions.reason: As in 18:16 and 25:9: people who passed a destroyed place were appalled and whistled in shock and scorn (50:13).

decisions.choice: horror, hissing / horror, object of scorn / horror, something people mock
decisions.reason: The wording settled for this pair in Jeremiah. The Hebrew verse is a single line; Literal and Balanced divide it once because it is long, and Readable keeps it as one line.

source.text: יַחְדָּ֖ו כַּכְּפִרִ֣ים יִשְׁאָ֑גוּ נָעֲר֖וּ כְּגוֹרֵ֥י אֲרָיֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Together like young lions they roar; they growl like cubs of lions.

en.L: Together they roar like young lions; \q they growl like lions' cubs.
en.B: They roar together like young lions; \q they growl like lion cubs.
en.R: The people of Babylon roar together like young lions. \q They growl like hungry lion cubs.

decisions.choice: they roar ... they growl: the Babylonians, greedy for prey
decisions.reason: The verse most likely describes the Babylonians themselves: like lions roaring over their kill, they are eager to devour (compare 2:15; 50:17). Verse 39 turns their hunger into a feast that ends in death. Some read the lions as the attackers, but "them" in verse 39 points back to these lions as the ones made drunk.

decisions.choice: The people of Babylon; hungry
decisions.reason: Readable names who roars (m1) and adds "hungry" to explain why lions roar and growl here.

source.text: בְּחֻמָּ֞ם אָשִׁ֣ית אֶת־מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֗ם וְהִשְׁכַּרְתִּים֙ לְמַ֣עַן יַעֲלֹ֔זוּ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In their being heated I will set their feast and I will make them drunk so that they exult, and they will sleep a sleep of forever and not wake, declares Yahweh.

en.L: When they are heated, I will set out their feast \q and make them drunk, so that they exult, \q and they will sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: While they are heated with greed, I will set out a feast for them \q and make them drunk, so that they shout and laugh, \q and they will sleep a sleep that lasts forever and never wake, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: While they are hot with hunger, I will set out a feast for them. \q I will make them drunk, and they will celebrate. \q Then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: when they are heated: in the heat of their greed or of their drinking
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow hot. It may mean the heat of the lions' hunger (verse 38) or the flush of wine at a feast (Hosea 7:5-7).

decisions.choice: I will set out their feast and make them drunk: the cup of judgment as a deadly banquet
decisions.reason: The LORD himself prepares the feast. Babylon, who made the nations drunk (verse 7), now drinks the cup of his wrath (25:15-16, 27). The story of Babylon's fall during a royal banquet (Daniel 5:1-4, 30) fits the picture.

decisions.choice: sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake: die
decisions.reason: Sleep from which there is no waking is death (Psalm 13:4; Job 14:12). The same words return in verse 57.

decisions.choice: so that they exult: the Greek reads "so that they are stunned"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they will exult, the noisy joy of drinkers, just before they fall into the sleep of death. The Greek translation reads "so that they may be stupefied", which may reflect a Hebrew verb of similar letters meaning "faint" (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: a sleep that lasts forever and never wake (B); fall asleep forever and never wake up (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording is used at each level in verse 57. Balanced adds "with greed" to show what the heat is (m1); Readable says "hunger".

source.text: אֽוֹרִידֵ֖ם כְּכָרִ֣ים לִטְב֑וֹחַ כְּאֵילִ֖ים עִם־עַתּוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter, like rams with male goats.

en.L: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, \q like rams together with male goats.
en.B: I will lead them down like lambs to be slaughtered, \q like rams and male goats.
en.R: I will lead them away like lambs to be killed, \q like rams and goats.

decisions.choice: lambs, rams, male goats: animals led to sacrifice
decisions.reason: The animals are those offered in sacrifice (Isaiah 34:6; Ezekiel 39:18). Babylon's people, the lions of verse 38, are now led down like tame sheep to be killed (11:19; 50:27).

source.text: אֵ֚יךְ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה שֵׁשַׁ֔ךְ וַתִּתָּפֵ֖שׂ תְּהִלַּ֣ת כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: How has been captured Sheshach, and has been seized [the] praise of all the earth! How has become a horror Babylon among the nations!

en.L: How Sheshach has been captured, \q and the praise of all the earth seized! \q How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
en.B: How Sheshach is taken, \q the pride of the whole earth seized! \q How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
en.R: Sheshach, that is, Babylon, has been captured! \q The city that the whole world praised has been taken! \q Babylon has become a horror among the nations!

decisions.choice: Sheshach: a coded name for Babylon
decisions.reason: As in 25:26, Sheshach is Babylon written in the code called *atbash*. Here it stands in parallel with "Babylon" in the next line, which shows what it means. The Greek translation lacks the name here (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: the praise of all the earth: the city all the world admired
decisions.reason: Babylon was the glory and pride of the nations (Isaiah 13:19). The same words are used of Jerusalem in 49:25 and Zephaniah 3:19.

decisions.choice: How ...!: a cry of astonishment, as in a lament
decisions.reason: The word opens a lament over a fall that seemed impossible (Isaiah 14:4, 12; Lamentations 1:1).

decisions.choice: Sheshach, that is, Babylon; The city that the whole world praised
decisions.reason: As in 25:26, Readable adds what the coded name stands for. It turns the exclamations into plain statements.

source.text: עָלָ֥ה עַל־בָּבֶ֖ל הַיָּ֑ם בַּהֲמ֥וֹן גַּלָּ֖יו נִכְסָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has gone up over Babylon the sea; with [the] roar of its waves she has been covered.

en.L: The sea has gone up over Babylon; \q she has been covered with the roar of its waves.
en.B: The sea has risen over Babylon; \q she is covered by its roaring waves.
en.R: An army like the sea has risen over Babylon. \q She is covered with its roaring waves.

decisions.choice: the sea ... its waves: the invading army as a flood
decisions.reason: A great army is often pictured as a flood (46:7-8; 47:2; Isaiah 8:7-8). Babylon, whose own sea the LORD will dry up (verse 36), is drowned by a greater sea: the nations sent against her.

decisions.choice: An army like the sea
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sea stands for (m1).

source.text: הָי֤וּ עָרֶ֨יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה אֶ֖רֶץ צִיָּ֣ה וַעֲרָבָ֑ה אֶ֗רֶץ לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֤ב בָּהֵן֙ כָּל־אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֥ר בָּהֵ֖ן בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Have become her cities a horror, a land of drought and desert, a land not dwells in them any man, and not passes through them a son of man.

en.L: Her cities have become a horror, \q a land of drought and desert, \q a land in which no one dwells, \q and through which no son of man passes.
en.B: Her towns have become a horror, \q a dry land and a desert, \q a land where no one lives, \q where no human being passes through.
en.R: Babylon's towns have become empty ruins. \q The land is dry like a desert. \q No one lives there. \q No one even travels through it.

decisions.choice: a horror: a ruin that appalls those who see it
decisions.reason: The word means both desolation and the shock it causes (verse 37). Babylon's well-watered land becomes a desert, as Jerusalem's did (2:6; 4:26-27).

decisions.choice: son of man: a human being
decisions.reason: The phrase means any human being (49:18, 33; 50:40). Not even a traveler will pass through.

decisions.choice: towns; human being
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "towns" for the many smaller places, as in 9:10, and "human being" for "son of man" (m2). Readable says "empty ruins" for "horror" here, where the sense is the ruin itself.

source.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עַל־בֵּ֜ל בְּבָבֶ֗ל וְהֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶת־בִּלְעוֹ֙ מִפִּ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יִנְהֲר֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו ע֖וֹד גּוֹיִ֑ם גַּם־חוֹמַ֥ת בָּבֶ֖ל נָפָֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out what he swallowed from his mouth, and not will stream to him again nations; also [the] wall of Babylon has fallen.

en.L: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, \q and nations will no longer stream to him; \q even the wall of Babylon has fallen.
en.B: I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed. \q Nations will stream to him no more; \q even Babylon's wall has fallen.
en.R: I will punish Bel, the god of Babylon. I will make him spit out what he swallowed. \q The nations will not come in crowds to worship him any more. \q Even the wall of Babylon has fallen.

decisions.choice: Bel: Marduk, the chief god of Babylon
decisions.reason: Bel means "lord" and was a title of Marduk, Babylon's patron god (50:2; Isaiah 46:1).

decisions.choice: bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed: Babylon must give back what she took
decisions.reason: In verse 34 Zion says that Nebuchadrezzar swallowed her like a sea monster. Now the LORD makes Babylon's god give back what he swallowed: the people and treasures taken from the nations, among them the exiles and the vessels of the temple (27:16-22; 52:17-23; Ezra 1:7-11).

decisions.choice: nations will no longer stream to him: Babylon will no longer draw the peoples
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the nations streaming to Zion (Isaiah 2:2; Jeremiah 31:12). The crowds of worshipers and tribute-bearers who flowed to Bel's city will stop.

decisions.choice: the Greek translation lacks the words from here to the middle of verse 49
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah, which is shorter than the Hebrew throughout (1:1), does not have the text from "nations will no longer stream to him" in this verse to "the slain of Israel" in verse 49 (this is from general knowledge). The Hebrew text is translated here in full.

decisions.choice: the god of Babylon; come in crowds to worship him
decisions.reason: Readable explains who Bel is (m1) and what the streaming of the nations means (m3).

source.text: צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י וּמַלְּט֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֑וֹ מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Go out from her midst, my people, and save each his life from [the] burning anger of Yahweh.

en.L: Go out from her midst, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and save your lives, each one, from the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Come out of her, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people! \q Every one of you, run for your life from the fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: Come out of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people! \q Everyone, run for your life to escape {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s terrible anger!

decisions.choice: go out from her midst, my people: the call to the exiles to leave Babylon
decisions.reason: The call of verse 6 returns, now as the LORD's own word to "my people" (50:8; Isaiah 48:20; 52:11). Revelation 18:4 takes it up: "Come out of her, my people".

decisions.choice: the burning anger of the LORD: his fierce anger
decisions.reason: Literally "the burning of the nose of the LORD", a set phrase for his anger at its height (4:8, 26; 25:37-38).

decisions.choice: run for your life
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

source.text: וּפֶן־יֵרַ֤ךְ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְתִֽירְא֔וּ בַּשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה הַנִּשְׁמַ֣עַת בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּבָ֧א בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמוּעָ֗ה וְאַחֲרָ֤יו בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁמוּעָ֔ה וְחָמָ֣ס בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל עַל־מֹשֵֽׁל׃

records.literal_gloss: And lest grow faint your heart and you fear at the report heard in the land, and comes in a year the report and after it in a year the report, and violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.

en.L: And let not your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid \q at the report heard in the land, \q when a report comes in one year, and after it a report in [another] year, \q and violence [is] in the land, and ruler [rises] against ruler.
en.B: Do not lose heart or be afraid \q at the rumors heard in the land, \q one rumor this year, another the next, \q rumors of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.
en.R: Do not lose courage or be afraid \q when you hear news in the land. \q One year there will be one report, and the next year another. \q There will be violence in the land, and one ruler will fight against another.

decisions.choice: and lest your heart grow faint: do not lose heart
