decisions.reason: The verse warns the exiles not to be shaken by the news that comes before Babylon's end. The word "lest" carries on from the call of verse 45: go out, and do not be afraid.

decisions.choice: the report: news or rumors of unrest
decisions.reason: The word means news heard by word of mouth (10:22; 49:14, 23). Year after year rumors come of violence and of rulers fighting each other.

decisions.choice: ruler against ruler: struggles for power in Babylon
decisions.reason: After Nebuchadnezzar died in 562 BC, Babylon had four kings in seven years, two of them killed in plots, before the last king, Nabonidus. The words may refer to such unrest, or to wars between Babylon's rulers and their rivals.

decisions.choice: [another]; [is]; [rises]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words English needs. Balanced and Readable say "rumors" and "news" for the report (m2).

source.text: לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים וּפָקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־פְּסִילֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְכָל־אַרְצָ֖הּ תֵּב֑וֹשׁ וְכָל־חֲלָלֶ֖יהָ יִפְּל֥וּ בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore here days coming and I will punish [the] idols of Babylon, and all her land will be ashamed, and all her slain will fall in her midst.

en.L: Therefore, look, days are coming \q when I will punish the idols of Babylon; \q her whole land will be put to shame, \q and all her slain will fall in her midst.
en.B: Therefore the days are coming \q when I will punish Babylon's idols. \q Her whole land will be put to shame, \q and all her slain will fall within her.
en.R: So the time is coming \q when I will punish Babylon's idols. \q Her whole land will be ashamed, \q and her people will lie dead everywhere in the city.

decisions.choice: punish the idols: deal with the carved gods of Babylon
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit and settle accounts (verse 18). The idols are the carved images of Babylon's gods (50:2, 38). Verse 52 repeats the line.

decisions.choice: put to shame: disgraced when its gods fail
decisions.reason: Those who trusted in the idols are shamed when the idols cannot save them (verse 17; 10:14).

decisions.choice: look, days are coming (L); the days are coming (B); the time is coming (R)
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording used elsewhere in Jeremiah (7:32; 16:14; 23:5).

source.text: וְרִנְּנ֤וּ עַל־בָּבֶל֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֔רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם כִּ֧י מִצָּפ֛וֹן יָבוֹא־לָ֥הּ הַשּׁוֹדְדִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will shout for joy over Babylon heaven and earth and all that [is] in them, for from [the] north will come to her the destroyers, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And heaven and earth and all that [is] in them \q will shout for joy over Babylon, \q for from the north the destroyers will come against her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then heaven and earth and everything in them \q will sing for joy over Babylon, \q for destroyers will come against her from the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then the sky and the earth and everything in them \q will shout for joy because of what happens to Babylon. \q Armies will come from the north and destroy her, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth will shout for joy: all creation rejoices at Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: Heaven and earth are called to rejoice at what God does (Isaiah 44:23; 49:13). Revelation 18:20 takes up the scene: "Rejoice over her, heaven".

decisions.choice: from the north ... the destroyers: the armies from the northern lands
decisions.reason: Judah's destroyer once came "from the north" (1:14; 4:6; 6:1). Now Babylon's destroyers come from the north too: the Medes and the peoples of verse 27 (50:3, 9, 41).

decisions.choice: Armies will come ... and destroy her
decisions.reason: Readable says "armies" for the destroyers, since verses 27-28 have named them.

source.text: גַּם־בָּבֶ֕ל לִנְפֹּ֖ל חַֽלְלֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גַּם־לְבָבֶ֥ל נָפְל֖וּ חַֽלְלֵ֥י כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also Babylon [is] to fall, [O] slain of Israel, as also for Babylon have fallen [the] slain of all the earth.

en.L: Babylon too must fall, \q for the slain of Israel, \q just as for Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.
en.B: Babylon must fall \q because of Israel's slain, \q just as because of Babylon the slain of the whole earth have fallen.
en.R: Babylon killed people all over the world. \q She killed the people of Israel too. \q Now Babylon herself must fall.

decisions.choice: Babylon must fall for the slain of Israel: her fall pays for those she killed
alternatives: Babylon too must fall, O slain of Israel
decisions.reason: The two halves are joined by "also ... also", setting Babylon's fall beside the deaths she caused: as the nations' dead fell because of Babylon, so Babylon must fall because of Israel's dead. The words "slain of Israel" could also be a call to the dead, "Babylon too must fall, O slain of Israel", but the parallel with "for Babylon" favors "for the slain of Israel".

decisions.choice: the Greek lacks the first half of this verse
decisions.reason: As noted at verse 44, the Greek translation lacks the text from verse 44b to "the slain of Israel" here (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: Babylon killed people all over the world ... Now Babylon herself must fall
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the comparison in the order of events, so the reason for Babylon's fall comes first.

source.text: פְּלֵטִ֣ים מֵחֶ֔רֶב הִלְכ֖וּ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ זִכְר֤וּ מֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם תַּעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [O] escapees from [the] sword, go, do not stand; remember from afar Yahweh, and Jerusalem let it come up on your heart.

en.L: You who have escaped the sword, \q go, do not stand still! \q Remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from afar, \q and let Jerusalem come up into your heart.
en.B: You who have escaped the sword, \q go! Do not linger! \q Remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in that distant land, \q and let Jerusalem come to your mind.
en.R: You who did not die in the war, \q leave Babylon! Do not wait! \q You are far from home, but remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Think about Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: you who have escaped the sword: the exiles of Judah who survived
decisions.reason: The survivors are those of Judah who lived through the wars and were carried to Babylon (44:28). They are told to leave as Babylon falls (verses 6, 45).

decisions.choice: remember the LORD from afar; let Jerusalem come up into your heart
decisions.reason: "From afar" means from the far country of exile (30:10; Zechariah 10:9). To have something "come up on the heart" is to think of it and long for it (3:16; Psalm 137:5-6).

decisions.choice: come to your mind (B); Think about (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2). Literal keeps "come up into your heart".

source.text: בֹּ֚שְׁנוּ כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ חֶרְפָּ֔ה כִּסְּתָ֥ה כְלִמָּ֖ה פָּנֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֚י בָּ֣אוּ זָרִ֔ים עַֽל־מִקְדְּשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: We are ashamed, for we have heard insult; has covered disgrace our faces, for have come strangers into [the] sanctuaries of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: "We are ashamed, for we have heard insult; \q disgrace has covered our faces, \q for strangers have come \q into the sanctuaries of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house."
en.B: "We are ashamed, for we have heard insults; \q disgrace covers our faces, \q because foreigners have gone into \q the holy places of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house."
en.R: "We are ashamed, because people insult us. \q Our faces show our shame, \q because foreigners have gone \q into the holy places of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple."

decisions.choice: we are ashamed: the exiles answer
decisions.reason: The exiles told to remember Jerusalem (verse 50) reply: they cannot think of it without shame, for the temple has been defiled. The LORD answers them in verse 52 with "Therefore".

decisions.choice: strangers have come into the sanctuaries: foreigners entered the holy places, which the law forbade
decisions.reason: Only priests could enter the holy rooms of the temple, and no foreigner could come into the sanctuary (Numbers 18:7; Ezekiel 44:7-9). The Babylonians went in, looted and burned it (52:13, 17-23; Lamentations 1:10; Psalm 79:1). "Sanctuaries" is plural, for the temple's holy rooms and courts.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the exiles' words
decisions.reason: The exiles' reply is speech quoted inside the oracle, so it takes double quotation marks.

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה־יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֖י עַל־פְּסִילֶ֑יהָ וּבְכָל־אַרְצָ֖הּ יֶאֱנֹ֥ק חָלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore here days coming, declares Yahweh, and I will punish her idols, and through all her land will groan [the] wounded.

en.L: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will punish her idols, \q and through all her land the wounded will groan.
en.B: Therefore the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will bring punishment on her idols, \q and the dying will groan in every part of her land.
en.R: So the time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will punish Babylon's idols. \q All over her land, wounded people will groan.

decisions.choice: days are coming when I will punish her idols: as verse 47
decisions.reason: The words of verse 47 return as the LORD's answer to the exiles' shame: Babylon's gods, who seemed to have won over the LORD's house, will be judged.

decisions.choice: the wounded will groan: those fatally wounded moan as they die
decisions.reason: The word means one pierced and dying (verse 4; Ezekiel 26:15). Babylon's land will be filled with the groans of the dying, as Jerusalem was.

decisions.choice: as verse 47
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording of verse 47.

source.text: כִּֽי־תַעֲלֶ֤ה בָבֶל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכִ֥י תְבַצֵּ֖ר מְר֣וֹם עֻזָּ֑הּ מֵאִתִּ֗י יָבֹ֧אוּ שֹׁדְדִ֛ים לָ֖הּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Though should go up Babylon [to] the heavens, and though she should fortify [the] height of her strength, from me will come destroyers to her, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Though Babylon should go up to the heavens, \q and though she should fortify her strong height, \q from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} destroyers will come to her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Even if Babylon should climb to the heavens \q and make her lofty stronghold secure, \q I will send destroyers against her, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Babylon may build her walls as high as the sky. \q She may make her high towers strong. \q But I will still send armies to destroy her, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: go up to the heavens: Babylon's pride, like the tower of Babel
decisions.reason: The words recall the builders of Babel, who wanted a tower with its top in the heavens (Genesis 11:4), and the king of Babylon who said, "I will go up to the heavens" (Isaiah 14:13-14). No height can keep the LORD's destroyers out (49:16; Obadiah 4).

decisions.choice: from me: sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The destroyers come "from with me", that is, at the LORD's command.

decisions.choice: I will send destroyers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I will send" for "from me ... will come" (m2).

source.text: ק֥וֹל זְעָקָ֖ה מִבָּבֶ֑ל וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּד֖וֹל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sound of a cry from Babylon, and great destruction from [the] land of [the] Chaldeans!

en.L: The sound of a cry from Babylon, \q and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
en.B: Listen! A cry rises from Babylon, \q the crash of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
en.R: Listen! People in Babylon are crying out. \q There is a great crash of destruction in the land of Babylonia.

decisions.choice: the sound of a cry ... great destruction: a cry of distress and the crash of ruin
decisions.reason: The first word can mean "sound" or serve as an exclamation, "Listen!" The cry is a scream for help; "destruction" is literally "breaking", a crash of ruin (4:6; 48:3, 5; 50:22, where nearly the same words are said of the land).

decisions.choice: Listen!
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the first word as an exclamation, which carries over to the second half (m1).

source.text: כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־בָּבֶ֔ל וְאִבַּ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וְהָמ֤וּ גַלֵּיהֶם֙ כְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים נִתַּ֥ן שְׁא֖וֹן קוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For [is] destroying Yahweh Babylon, and he will make perish from her [the] great voice; and roar their waves like many waters; is given [the] uproar of their voice.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying Babylon, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will silence her great voice; \q and their waves roar like many waters; \q the uproar of their voice resounds.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying Babylon \q and silencing her loud noise. \q Their waves roar like mighty waters; \q the din of their voices rises.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is destroying Babylon. \q He will make her loud noise go silent. \q The enemy armies roar like great ocean waves. \q Their shouting grows louder and louder.

decisions.choice: silence her great voice: put an end to the noise of the busy city
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or make perish, and with "voice" it means to silence. The "great voice" is the noise of a crowded city, its trade and its celebrations (7:34; 25:10).

decisions.choice: their waves roar like many waters: the attacking armies come like a raging sea
decisions.reason: "Their" most likely refers to the attackers, pictured again as a sea (verse 42; Isaiah 17:12-13). Babylon's noise is silenced, and the noise of the invaders takes its place.

decisions.choice: The enemy armies
decisions.reason: Readable names whose waves these are (m2).

source.text: כִּי֩ בָ֨א עָלֶ֤יהָ עַל־בָּבֶל֙ שׁוֹדֵ֔ד וְנִלְכְּדוּ֙ גִּבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ חִתְּתָ֖ה קַשְּׁתוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֧ל גְּמֻל֛וֹת יְהוָ֖ה שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For has come against her, against Babylon, a destroyer, and are captured her warriors; are shattered their bows; for a God of recompenses [is] Yahweh; repaying he will repay.

en.L: For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon, \q and her warriors are captured, \q their bows are shattered, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a God of recompense; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will surely repay.
en.B: For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. \q Her warriors are captured, \q their bows are broken, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a God who repays; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay in full.
en.R: A destroyer has come to attack Babylon. \q Her soldiers are captured. \q Their bows are broken. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is a God who gives people what they deserve. He will pay Babylon back in full.

decisions.choice: a God of recompense: the LORD gives each what their deeds deserve
decisions.reason: The plural noun is from the root of "recompense" in verse 6 and "repay" here. The LORD is a God who repays: he does not leave wrong unanswered (Deuteronomy 32:35, 41; Isaiah 59:18). The doubled verb, "repaying he will repay", makes the promise certain and complete.

decisions.choice: their bows are shattered: the army's weapons broken
decisions.reason: The bow stands for a nation's military strength (49:35; Hosea 1:5). The archers of verse 3 now lose their bows.

decisions.choice: will surely repay (L); will repay in full (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level renders the doubled verb (m1) with a word of emphasis.

source.text: וְ֠הִשְׁכַּרְתִּי שָׂרֶ֨יהָ וַחֲכָמֶ֜יהָ פַּחוֹתֶ֤יהָ וּסְגָנֶ֨יהָ֙ וְגִבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֨ם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her officials and her warriors, and they will sleep a sleep of forever and not wake, declares the King, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.

en.L: And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her officials and her warriors, \q and they will sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake, \q declares the King, \q whose name [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: I will make her officials and wise men drunk, her governors, deputies and warriors, \q and they will sleep a sleep that lasts forever and never wake, \q declares the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: I will make her leaders and wise men drunk, and her governors, officials and soldiers. \q Then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, \q says the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: make drunk ... sleep a perpetual sleep: the words of verse 39 return
decisions.reason: The feast of verse 39 is now given to Babylon's leaders. All the ranks of her rulers drink the LORD's cup and die. The words are those of verse 39.

decisions.choice: the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts: the true king above the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: The title answers the "king of Babylon" (verses 31, 34). The LORD is the King of all the earth (10:7, 10; 46:18; 48:15).

decisions.choice: princes, governors, officials: the ranks of the empire's rulers
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, governors and officials are titles of the empire's provincial rulers; princes are the court's leading men.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); her officials (L), deputies (B), officials (R)
decisions.reason: *Sar* follows the settled wording: "princes", "officials", "leaders". Since Balanced already uses "officials" for *sar*, it says "deputies" for the second title, which is "officials" in verse 23. The words about sleep keep the wording of verse 39 at each level.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת חֹ֠מוֹת בָּבֶ֤ל הָֽרְחָבָה֙ עַרְעֵ֣ר תִּתְעַרְעָ֔ר וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ הַגְּבֹהִ֖ים בָּאֵ֣שׁ יִצַּ֑תּוּ וְיִֽגְע֨וּ עַמִּ֧ים בְּדֵי־רִ֛יק וּלְאֻמִּ֥ים בְּדֵי־אֵ֖שׁ וְיָעֵֽפוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: [The] walls of Babylon, the broad, utterly will be laid bare, and her gates, the high, with fire will be burned; and toil peoples for nothing, and nations for fire, and they grow weary.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: The broad wall of Babylon will be utterly laid bare, \q and her high gates will be burned with fire; \q and peoples toil for nothing, and nations for fire, and they grow weary.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: The broad wall of Babylon will be leveled to the ground, \q and her high gates will be set on fire. \q The peoples toil for nothing; the nations wear themselves out only for the fire.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down. \q Her tall gates will be burned. \q The people of the nations worked hard to build them, but it was all for nothing. They wore themselves out, only for it all to burn.

decisions.choice: the broad wall ... utterly laid bare: Babylon's great walls razed to their foundations
decisions.reason: The noun is plural, "walls", for the whole system of walls, with a singular adjective "broad". Babylon's double walls were famous for their width. The doubled verb means to strip to the ground, to raze completely.

decisions.choice: peoples toil for nothing, nations for fire: the same saying as Habakkuk 2:13
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 2:13 has almost the same words in the reverse order: "peoples toil for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing". It is a saying about empires built by forced labor: all their work ends in flames. Habakkuk has not yet been translated in this project; when it is, the two should be compared. The last verb, "and they grow weary", returns at the end of verse 64.

decisions.choice: for nothing: for the sake of emptiness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "for enough of emptiness", that is, their labor gains them nothing but emptiness, and "enough of fire", only enough to feed the flames.

decisions.choice: utterly laid bare (L); leveled to the ground (B); completely torn down (R); wear themselves out only for the fire (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the doubled verb means (m1) and make the last line clear. Readable adds that the peoples built the walls, which the saying implies.

source.text: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה׀יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא אֶת־שְׂרָיָ֣ה בֶן־נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה֒ בְּלֶכְתּ֞וֹ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה שַׂ֥ר מְנוּחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The word that commanded Jeremiah the prophet Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah in his going with Zedekiah king of Judah [to] Babylon in the fourth year of his reigning; and Seraiah [was] officer of [the] resting place.

en.L: The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah [was] officer of the resting place.
en.B: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave as a command to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
en.R: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah and grandson of Mahseiah. Seraiah was going to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah. This was in Zedekiah's fourth year as king. Seraiah was the officer in charge of the places where the king stopped to rest on the journey.

decisions.choice: Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah: the brother of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe
decisions.reason: Baruch is "son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah" (32:12; 36:4), so Seraiah, with the same father and grandfather, was his brother. One brother wrote down Jeremiah's words in Jerusalem; the other carried his word against Babylon to Babylon itself.

decisions.choice: with Zedekiah ... in the fourth year of his reign: about 594 BC
decisions.reason: Zedekiah's fourth year is the year of chapters 27-28, when envoys of other kings met in Jerusalem to plan revolt against Babylon. A journey to Babylon that year may have been to assure Nebuchadrezzar of Judah's loyalty. The trip is not mentioned elsewhere. The Greek translation reads "from Zedekiah", making Seraiah the king's envoy rather than his companion (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: officer of the resting place: probably the quartermaster, in charge of the stops on the journey
alternatives: officer in charge of the tribute
decisions.reason: The title means "officer of the resting place" and is found only here. It most likely names the official who arranged where the king's party would halt and lodge on the way. Its exact meaning is uncertain. The Greek translation reads "officer of gifts", from Hebrew letters close to those of "tribute" (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: the word that Jeremiah commanded: a closing story in prose
decisions.reason: After the long poem against Babylon (50:1-51:58), the book tells how Jeremiah sent it to Babylon. These verses are prose narrative.

decisions.choice: quartermaster (B); the officer in charge of the places where the king stopped to rest (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the familiar title for the officer who arranged lodging on a march; Readable explains it. Literal keeps the Hebrew words. Readable says "grandson of Mahseiah", as in 32:12.

source.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אֵ֧ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־תָּב֥וֹא אֶל־בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־סֵ֣פֶר אֶחָ֑ד אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה הַכְּתֻבִ֖ים אֶל־בָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And wrote Jeremiah all the disaster that would come to Babylon in one scroll, all the words these that are written concerning Babylon.

en.L: And Jeremiah wrote in one scroll all the disaster that would come on Babylon, all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
en.B: Jeremiah had written on a single scroll all the disaster that would come on Babylon, all these words written about Babylon.
en.R: Jeremiah had written on one scroll about all the disasters that would happen to Babylon. He wrote all the words that are written above about Babylon.

decisions.choice: all these words written concerning Babylon: the oracle of chapters 50-51
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean the poem just given (50:1-51:58), or the heart of it. The scroll is "one" because it was written for this single purpose, to be read and sunk in Babylon.

decisions.choice: wrote: had written, before Seraiah set out
decisions.reason: The verb tells what Jeremiah did to prepare for Seraiah's journey; the order of events allows "had written".

decisions.choice: written above
decisions.reason: Readable says "above" to make clear that the words are those of the preceding chapters (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־שְׂרָיָ֑ה כְּבֹאֲךָ֣ בָבֶ֔ל וְֽרָאִ֔יתָ וְֽקָרָ֔אתָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to Seraiah: When you come [to] Babylon, and you will see, and you will read all the words these,

en.L: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you come to Babylon, see [to it] that you read all these words aloud,
en.B: Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you reach Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud,
en.R: Jeremiah told Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, make sure you read all these words out loud.

decisions.choice: and you will see, and you will read: see to it that you read
decisions.reason: The two verbs together mean "take care to read" (compare Exodus 25:40). It may also mean "look around you and read": read where the city can be seen.

decisions.choice: read aloud: proclaim the words in Babylon itself
decisions.reason: The verb means to read aloud. Whether many heard it or Seraiah read it for God alone, the word against Babylon was spoken in Babylon, as a prophetic act (verse 63).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes in verse 64
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's instructions run to the end of verse 64; the words Seraiah is to say take single quotation marks. Readable ends the sentence here.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ יְהוָה֙ אַתָּ֨ה דִבַּ֜רְתָּ אֶל־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ לְהַכְרִית֔וֹ לְבִלְתִּ֤י הֱיֽוֹת־בּוֹ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֔ב לְמֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה כִּֽי־שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will say: Yahweh, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that not [is] in it an inhabitant, from man to beast, for desolations of forever it will be.

en.L: and say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that there will be no one dwelling in it, from human to animal, for it will be a desolation forever.'
en.B: and say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy this place, so that nothing will live in it, neither people nor animals, and it will be a desolation forever.'
en.R: Then say, '{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy this place. No people or animals will live here. It will be an empty ruin forever.'

decisions.choice: to cut it off ... from human to animal ... a desolation forever: the words of the oracle
decisions.reason: Seraiah repeats the oracle's own sentence: no one living there, human or animal (50:3; 51:29, 43), and a desolation forever (51:26). He holds God to his word in the place it concerns.

decisions.choice: LORD, you have spoken: Seraiah speaks to God
decisions.reason: The words are a prayer addressed to the LORD, not a message to the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: What Seraiah is to say is quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, so it takes single quotation marks. The LORD is addressed without "O", as in Isaiah.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ כְּכַלֹּ֣תְךָ֔ לִקְרֹ֖א אֶת־הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה תִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ אֶ֔בֶן וְהִשְׁלַכְתּ֖וֹ אֶל־תּ֥וֹךְ פְּרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be when you finish to read this scroll, you will tie on it a stone and you will throw it into [the] midst of [the] Euphrates,

en.L: And when you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
en.B: When you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
en.R: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it. Throw it into the middle of the Euphrates River.

decisions.choice: tie a stone to it and throw it: an acted sign of Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: Like the loincloth of 13:1-11 and the broken jar of 19:1-13, the act shows what the words say: as the scroll sinks, so will Babylon (verse 64). Revelation 18:21 takes up the sign: an angel throws a great millstone into the sea and says Babylon will be thrown down like it.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates: the river of Babylon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the river, Perath, the Euphrates, which ran through the city of Babylon (13:4; 46:2).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the river's name here, not "the River", so every level says "the Euphrates"; Readable adds "River".

records.literal_gloss: and you will say: Thus will sink Babylon and not rise because of the disaster that I [am] bringing on her, and they will grow weary. Until here [are the] words of Jeremiah.

en.L: and say, 'Thus Babylon will sink and not rise, because of the disaster that I am bringing on her, and they will grow weary.'" Thus far [are] the words of Jeremiah.
en.B: and say, 'So Babylon will sink and rise no more, because of the disaster I am bringing on her, and they will grow weary.'" Here the words of Jeremiah end.
en.R: Then say, 'In the same way Babylon will sink and never come up again, because of the disaster I am bringing on her. And they will grow weary.'" This is the end of Jeremiah's words.

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary: probably a phrase repeated by mistake from verse 58
alternatives: part of what Seraiah is to say
decisions.reason: The words end verse 58, where they make sense: the nations wear themselves out for nothing. Here they do not fit the sentence. They may have been copied as a marker of where the poem ended, before the story of verses 59-64 was placed after it, and then left in the text. The Greek translation lacks them (this is from general knowledge). They are kept here because they are in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: I am bringing: the LORD's own words, spoken by Seraiah
decisions.reason: Seraiah's words turn into the LORD's own word, as the prophet's message does elsewhere: the "I" is the LORD.

decisions.choice: thus far the words of Jeremiah: the end of the book's collection of his words
decisions.reason: The note marks the end of Jeremiah's words. Chapter 52 is an appendix from the history of the kings, nearly the same as 2 Kings 24:18-25:30, telling of Jerusalem's fall and of King Jehoiachin's release in Babylon. It shows that Jeremiah's word came true. The Greek translation lacks this note (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary kept inside Seraiah's words; the quotation closes
decisions.reason: The phrase stands where the Hebrew has it (m1), at the end of the quoted words. Readable sets it as a sentence of its own. Jeremiah's speech, opened in verse 61, closes here, before the closing note.
